science.title: Light-induced asymmetric pseudogap below the critical temperature in cuprates
science.description: High-temperature cuprate superconductors remain a key platform for studying the competition and coexistence of emergent quantum phases of matter. These include non-s-wave superconductivity with a high transition temperature, non-Fermi-liquid transport and the pseudogap regime. How superconductivity emerges alongside and competes with the pseudogap remains an open question. Here, by directly accessing the near-antinodal region of optimally doped Bi-based cuprates via time- and angle-resolved photoemission, we report a transient change from a symmetric superconducting-like density of states to an asymmetric pseudogap-like density of states when superconductivity is disrupted by a sufficiently high excitation fluence. We observe this change at electronic temperatures well below the equilibrium superconducting critical temperature. Conversely, when superconductivity is fully restored, the pseudogap is suppressed, as indicated by a particle–hole-symmetric density of states. We also observe the coexistence of pseudogap and superconducting features at intermediate times or intermediate fluence. Our findings challenge the view that superconductivity emerges from phase coherence in the pseudogap. Instead, we show that the two states compete and that the low-temperature ground state of cuprates reflects an interplay between the superconducting and pseudogap states. How superconductivity relates to the pseudogap in cuprates remains unclear. Now, time-resolved photoemission measurements show a light-induced pseudogap-like state below critical temperature, revealing a dynamic interplay with superconductivity.

science.title: Lagrangian-Eulerian learning of flow field and trajectories with TrajectoryFlowNet
science.description: Predicting particle transport in complex flows is traditionally achieved by solving the Navier–Stokes equations. Numerical and experimental methods typically require deep physical insights and incur high computational costs. Although machine learning offers an alternative, existing approaches fail to generalize the prediction of long-range particle trajectories in sparse data regimes. Here, to this end, we propose TrajectoryFlowNet, a Lagrangian–Eulerian physics-informed neural network architecture, for fluid flow velocimetry and imaging via learning to predict spatiotemporal flow fields and long-range particle trajectories. The salient features of our model include its ability to handle complex flow patterns with irregular boundaries, predict the full-field flows, image the long-range flow trajectory of any arbitrary particle, and ensure physical consistency in predictions based on only scarce measurement of flow trajectories. We validate TrajectoryFlowNet via both numerical examples (for example, lid-driven cavity flow and complex cylinder flow) and experimental test cases (for example, aortic and ventricle blood flows) across diverse flow scenarios. The results demonstrate our model’s effectiveness in capturing intricate particle-laden flow dynamics, enabling long-range tracking of particles and accurate construction of flow fields in real-world applications. Wan et al. introduce a physics-informed learning model that simultaneously predicts long-range particle paths and flow fields based on very limited trajectory measurements, validated in both simulations and blood-flow experiments.

science.title: Enhanced surface hydrophobicity in the combined treatment of chaplins and rodlins from Streptomyces griseus
science.description: Many microorganisms depend on their hydrophobic hyphal surfaces to grow into the air and disperse their spores. In Streptomyces species, this property is conferred by chaplin and rodlin proteins. In the present study, we examined the potential of chaplins and rodlins from Streptomyces griseus IFO 13350, focusing on their contributions to surface hydrophobicity. In vitro assays with recombinant chaplins (ChpC and ChpH) and rodlins (RdlA and RdlB) demonstrated that ChpH alone increased the hydrophobicity of glass slides. The combination of ChpH with RdlA/RdlB enhanced water repellency, yielding a contact angle of 66.7 ± 2.6°, which was significantly greater than that of either ChpH or RdlA/RdlB alone. The long chaplin, ChpC, did not show such an enhancement with RdlA/RdlB. Gene disruption experiments supported the assumption that short chaplin ChpH plays a dominant role in generating hydrophobic surfaces and acts cooperatively with RdlA and/or RdlB to produce strongly water-repellent surfaces. We showed that hydrophobicity can be maintained even in the absence of rodlet structures, highlighting the flexibility of the chaplin–rodlin system. Based on these findings, we propose a hypothetical model in which rodlins act as molecular scaffolds that align short-chaplin fibrils into ordered rodlet arrays, thereby amplifying surface hydrophobicity. This study also suggests that chaplins in combination with rodlins have potential as effective additives for surface hydrophobicity.

science.title: Experimental demonstration of attosecond hard X-ray pulses
science.description: We present the experimental confirmation of attosecond pulse generation in the hard X-ray regime with a free-electron laser. Our experiment is based on the measurements of a nonlinear optical phenomenon known as amplified spontaneous emission from 3d transition metals. By analysing the yield of the collective X-ray fluorescence induced by ultrashort pulses at the Linac Coherent Light Source, we identify the generation of attosecond pulses and shot-to-shot fluctuations in their duration, ranging from 100 as to 400 as. The inferred time–bandwidth product for 100-as pulses is approximately 2 fs eV, indicating that a fraction of the pulses is nearly transform-limited pulses. Our results confirm the generation of attosecond hard X-ray pulses that can be used to simultaneously probe matter on the timescales of electronic phenomena and with atomic spatial resolution. Furthermore, attosecond hard X-ray pulses can outrun the fastest radiation damage processes, paving the way to single-shot damage-free X-ray measurements. Researchers experimentally demonstrate attosecond pulse generation in the hard X-ray regime with a free-electron laser. The confirmation is enabled via the measurement of amplified spontaneous emission from 3d transition metals. Pulse durations are in the range of 100 as to 400 as.

science.title: Early lineage divergence segregates sensory and motor-associative identities in the thalamus
science.description: The thalamus integrates sensory, motor and associative functions through distinct nuclei, yet the developmental principles driving their specification remain unclear. Here we generate a spatiotemporal single-cell multiomic and spatial transcriptomic atlas of the embryonic mouse thalamus, combined with barcoding-based lineage tracing. We identify two major glutamatergic lineages, sensory-related and motor-associative, each governed by different gene regulatory programs and temporal dynamics. These lineages arise from spatially and molecularly distinct progenitor domains, revealing an early segregation of functional identities. Within the sensory lineage, we resolve branching sensory trajectories leading to first-order visual and somatosensory neurons, both emerging from a shared higher-order-like state. Using in silico predictions and in vivo perturbation, we identify Sp9 as a key regulator of visual thalamic fate. Together, our findings define the molecular architecture and developmental trajectories that underpin thalamic modality specification, providing a framework to understand how functional circuits emerge in the mammalian brain. Sensory and motor-associative identities in the thalamus arise from two early-diverging lineages, with sensory neurons progressing through shared intermediate states, revealing how thalamic organization emerges during development.
